title: Why Door Handles Shock You in Winter
caption:
That metal door handle zap is not bad luck.
A cartoon guy heads out for lunch, grabs the cold metal door handle, and a yellow spark cracks as he yelps that his hair knew the shock was coming; a diagram then labels the effect electrostatic induction, with hairs lifting under a voltage meter.
Your body builds up static charge as you shuffle across carpet or slide out of a chair, and when your hand nears the metal handle that charge is drawn to the surface before you even touch it; the tiny hairs on your skin stand up first, and the moment contact happens the charge jumps across in a spark you feel as a shock.
Have you ever felt your hair rise right before a door handle bit you?
Save this so you finally understand that winter zap, then follow for more everyday body science.
